title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No mathematical error is visible. The definition of the 'standard construction' and the precise form of the loop relation (exponent μ-1 on ε1) are on other pages, so they cannot be checked here.
The remark gives only a sufficient condition and is stated without proof (completed on the next page).

ideas.what: Functoriality of the automorphism/normaliser groups Z_{ρ,σ} and of the derived groups G_{ρ,σ}, G^𝔊_{ρ,σ} under surjections 𝔊 → 𝔊' whose kernel is stable under the relevant automorphisms
ideas.modern_name: functoriality of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type groups for characteristic (or stable) quotients of F̂_2, e.g. GT acting on nilpotent or pro-ℓ quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s), Lochak–Schneps for GT and its variants; pro-ℓ/nilpotent versions by Ihara and others
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller tower and the action of Gal(Q̄/Q) on it

ideas.what: Sufficient lifting condition: if solutions (α',β') of the loop equation in 𝔊' always come from automorphisms of 𝔊'^+, then every (ρ,σ)-morphism into 𝔊' is admissible
ideas.modern_name: rigidity/freeness property ensuring that GT-type parameters (λ,f) define automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in GT theory (Drinfeld; Ihara; Lochak–Schneps)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine functoriality bookkeeping inside Grothendieck's unpublished loop-equation framework. The remark is a standard lifting/rigidity criterion; nothing here appears to go beyond what GT theory later made explicit.
transcription_corrections: The group symbol on this page is the same curly 𝔊 used on the previous page, not 𝔖: read 𝔊^+, 𝔊'^+, L_0^𝔊, 𝔊'^𝔊_ε throughout.

Superscripts in (94)/(95) look misplaced. In the image (94) is G_{ρ,σ} → G_{ρ',σ'} (the target superscript is unclear), and (95) has the 𝔊 superscript on both source and target: G^𝔊_{ρ,σ} → G^𝔊_{ρ',σ'}, with map labelled φ_{G^𝔊}.
'(64) relatif : 𝔊(ρ,σ)': the 𝔊 is struck through, so read '(64) relatif à (ρ,σ)'.
The insertion above 'Supposons que 𝔊'' reads ', 𝔊'^𝔊,' (i.e. 𝔊' together with 𝔊'^𝔊), not 𝔖-symbols.
'Il n'en faut pas plus pour que toutes les constructions {de diagrammes} des nos précédents, relatives à ρ,σ, s'envoient dans celles relatives à ρ',σ'' is correct as read.
